DI P'UP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor Quezon Avenue. West Triangle. Quezon City www dilggy.ph OILG OPINION NO. (5 MAR 05 202b ENGR. NELSON G. LINGAT, DPA City Administrator City of San Fernando Province of Pampanga Dear Engr. Lingat: This has reference to your letter dated 12 December 2024 seeking this Department's guidance and legal opinion on the following matters: l. VNhether or not the ordinance is within the oversight powers of the provincial govemment, as provided under relevant laws; and 2. VVhether or not there is administrative contradiction or superfluity, given the concerned national government agencies' oversight over local counterparts and the current principle of avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy. Per the representation, the provincial government of Pampanga enacted Ordinance No. 878 entitled "An Ordinance Providing for the Oversight Functions of the Provincial Government on Matters Relating to the Issuance of Business Permits, Development permits, Environmental Clearances, Building Permits, Tax Clearances, Real Property Assessments, and other Clearances (oversight matters) issued by Barangays, Cities, and Municipalities within the Province of Pampanga." You then represented that while the city government acknowledges the supervisory functions of the provincial government, you would like to assert respect for its autonomy and presumption of the regular performance of its functionaries' duties. Thus, the request for legal opinion. As to the first query, we answer in the affirmative. Section 29 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Codes, provides that the provincial government has general supervisory powers over component cities and municipalities but not direct control. This means it may ensure that lower local government units (LGUs) to comply with the law but cannot interfere with their discretionary functions unless expressly provided by law. In connection with this, we are of the considered view that the subject ordinance merely provides oversight in terms of policy guidance, monitoring, and ensuring compliance with provincial and national regulations. The subject ordinance, specifically Sections 4 and 5, simply requires barangays, cities, and municipalities to submit a summary report of all oversight matters to the Regulatory Compliance Unit, with the unit's authority limited to recommending corrective actions, sanctions, or penalties for noncompliance. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The subject ordinance does not authorize the provincial government to interfere with the discretionary authority of cities and municipalities by requiring prior approval or imposing conditions that are not present in national laws. The ordinance likewise does not require prior approval or directly regulate the permits or clearances. Hence. the ordinance is within the oversight powers of the provincial government. As to the final query, we answer in the negative. Upon review of the subject ordinance, we are of the considered view that it does not grant the provincial government powers that are already exercised by National Govemment Agencies. There is nothing in the code that requires the provincial government to conduct its own review before a city or municipality issues a permit. The ordinance merely monitors compliance without interfering in the decision-making process. Thus, there is no administrative contradiction or superfluity on the subject ordinance. This opinion is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P. NITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELL.AJRPB/LLLS-LRALLD,'lasm copy furnished: ATTY. ANTHONY C.
